title: Πέρδιξ καὶ ἄνθρωπος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 300. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.l: A certain man, having caught a partridge, was about to cut its throat.
sentences.n: μέλλω with the infinitive is 'be on the point of'. σφάζω is the slaughtering-word, used of the knife drawn across the throat, whether at the altar or at the table.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ ἱκέτευε λέγουσα· « Ἔασόν με ζῆν καὶ ἀντ’ ἐμοῦ πολλὰς πέρδικας ἐγώ σοι κυνηγήσω. »
sentences.tr: Hē de hiketeue legousa· « Eason me zēn kai ant’ emou pollas perdikas egō soi kynēgēsō. »
sentences.l: But she kept entreating, saying: « Let me live, and in place of myself I will hunt many partridges for you. »
sentences.n: ἱκετεύω is the suppliant's word, used of one who has nothing but the appeal itself; the imperfect keeps the pleading going. ἀντ’ ἐμοῦ is 'in exchange for me', the language of a bargain. ἐγώ is written out where the verb ending would have done, and the emphasis is the whole of her offer. A tame partridge does the same service in fable 285, and is answered much as here.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· « Δι’ αὐτὸ τοῦτο μᾶλλόν σε θύσω, ὅτι τοὺς συνήθεις καὶ φίλους σοι ἐνεδρεῦσαι θέλεις. »
sentences.tr: Ho de eipen· « Di’ auto touto mallon se thysō, hoti tous synētheis kai philous soi enedreusai theleis. »
sentences.l: But he said: « For this very reason I will sacrifice you the more, because you are willing to lay an ambush for those who are companions and friends to you. »
sentences.i: But he said: « That is the very reason I shall be the readier to kill you: because you are willing to entrap your own companions and friends. »
sentences.n: θύω is to sacrifice, and a bird killed for the table was killed in the same way and with the same word. σοι is a dative of possession going with τοὺς συνήθεις καὶ φίλους: the companions and friends that are hers. ἐνεδρεύω is to lie in wait for a thing, the hunter's word turned against her.

sentences.t: Ὅτι ὁ κατὰ φίλων αὐτοῦ δολίας μηχανὰς συντιθεὶς αὐτὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐνέδραις τῶν κινδύνων ἐμπεσεῖται.
sentences.tr: Hoti ho kata philōn autou dolias mēchanas syntitheis autos en tais enedrais tōn kindynōn empeseitai.
sentences.l: That the man who puts together crafty contrivances against his own friends will himself fall into the ambushes of dangers.
sentences.i: The story shows that the man who puts together crafty contrivances against his own friends will himself fall into the ambushes of danger.
sentences.n: A moral in the bare Ὅτι form: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek and is supplied in the idiomatic line. συντίθημι is to set things together, and so to frame or contrive. ἐμπίπτω here takes ἐν with the dative rather than the commoner εἰς — the fall is pictured as happening inside the trap. αὐτοῦ does duty for ἑαυτοῦ, 'his own'.
